title: Macrophage-T Cell Coculture Model for Tissue Injury-Induced T Cell Death
author: Zhu, Cao, et al.
materials: All recipes can be found in “materials and equipment”.4.Bone marrow-derived macrophage mediuma.Mix DMEM (+GLutaMAX) with 10 % inactivated (56°C for 30 min) fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1 % Gentamycin (stock: 50 mg/mL).b.Before usage heat up to 37°C in water bath.5.Inflammasome stimulation mediuma.For stimulation of the BMDMs’ inflammasome, collect murine serum from mice which received an experimental stroke (Figure 1) and add it to BMDM medium. The final solution contains 25 % murine stroke serum.Figure 1Serum collection from mice with acute tissue injury(A) In our model mice received an experimental stroke (filament-induced occlusion of the middle cerebral artery (fMCAO; 60 min of ischemia)) and were then sacrificed 4 h after reperfusion (5 h after the start of the surgery). Mice were sacrificed and blood was drawn intracardially with a 24 gauge needle. Blood was stored in 1.5 mL protein-low binding tubes and kept for 30 min at room temperature (RT) for clotting. Tubes were then centrifuged at 3,500 g for 15 min. Serum (=supernatant) was then collected, aliquoted and immediately stored at −80°C until further usage.(B) Schematic of the circle of willis: For the model utilized in the manuscript, a silcon-coated mono filament was inserted in the common carotid artery (CCA) and pushed up (via the internal carotid artery (ICA)) to occlude the middle cerebral artery (MCA).(C) Representative cresyl violet staining of coronal brain sections. The healthy tissue is stained in violet, the lesion areas remain white.Abbreviations: ACA = anterior cerebral artery; BA = basiliar artery, CCA = common carotid artery, ECA = external carotid artery, PCA = posterior cerebral artery, PPA = Pterygopalatine artery.6.T cell mediuma.Mix RPMI 1640 complete with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1 % Penicillin/Streptomycin (Stock: 10,000 U/10,000 U)b.Before usage add β-mercaptoethanol to a final concentration of 5 nM and heat the medium up to 37°C.

In this step, splenic T cells will be enriched from murine spleen. This is achieved by using a magnetic bead-based commercial T cell negative selection kit. Make sure that you have prepared anti-CD3ε-coated 96-well plates before starting isolation. Coating with anti-CD3e antibody is essential for functional T cell culture.7.Spleen collection.a.Euthanize Bl6/J mouse, disinfect and fixate in supine position.b.Open the abdomen and expose the spleen from surrounding fat tissue.c.Remove the spleen and store in 10 mL of ice-cold PBS for transfer to laminar air flow.8.Collection, straining and enrichment of splenic T cells.Note: The T cell isolation was done with the MagniSort T cell enrichment kit (ThermoFisher, US; see key resources table). Volumes and incubation times are according to the manufacturer’s protocol.The used antibody cocktail contains: Anti-mouse CD11b, CD19, CD24, CD45R, CD49b, Ly6G and TER-119 according to the manufacturer’s data sheet. Using alternative kits for T cell enrichment/isolation is possible.a.Prepare conic 50 mL tube and 40 μm strainer.b.Mince the spleen using scissors and carefully press tissue through the 40 μm strainer with a syringe plunger while continuously rinsing with a least 10 mL PBSc.Fill up volume to at least 20 mL volume and wash the suspension at 300 g for 10 min at RT.d.Acquire cell numbers and titrate the concentration to 107 cells per 100 μL.e.Transfer the whole cell suspension into a 5 mL “FACS” tube (see key resources table)f.Add 20 μL of the T cell enrichment antibody cocktail (please see “Note” for the T cell enrichment kit) per 100 μL cell suspension, briefly vortex at least 3 times and incubate 10 min at RT. Red blood cell lysis is not required here, the antibody cocktail of the enrichment kit implements anti-TER-119, removing red blood cells.g.Bring the suspension volume up to 4 mL with Hank’s balanced salt solution (HBSS, see key resources table) and wash at 300 g for 8 min at RT.h.Discard supernatant and resuspend with 100 μL HBSS per 107 cells.i.Add 20 μL of the magnetic bead-labeled antibodies per 100 μL cell suspension, briefly vortex at least 3 times and incubate for 5 min at RT.j.Bring the volume up to 2.5 mL with HBSS and place the FACS tube into the supplied magnet (see “Note”) for 5 min at RT. In this critical step separation of magnetic bead-labeled immune cells and unlabeled T cells is conducted.k.Decant carefully the suspension from the “magnetized” tube into a fresh 4 mL FACS tube (=enriched T cells).Optional: Remove the remaining tube (= removed splenocytes, antibody-labeled) and use the cells for quality control via flow cytometry.9.Seeding T cells and initiation of proliferation.a.Wash the enriched T cells at 300 g for 8 min (RT).b.Acquire cell numbers and titrate to a concentration of 3 × 105 cells per 200 μL with T cell medium (see “before you begin”).c.Place 200 μL T cell suspension per well onto a U-bottom 96-well plate (pre-coated with CD3e antibody; see “before you begin” and key resources table).d.After letting the cells settle for 15 min add CD28 antibody (10 μL; 0.1 μg/μL) to the T cells.e.Place the cells overnight (12–18 h) into an incubator at 37°C for settling.f.Control the viability of the T cells before starting the coculture approach (Figure 1B).

steps.title: Prepare plates, tools and consumables
steps.instruction: Coat 96‑well U‑bottom plates with anti‑CD3ε antibody overnight at 4 °C (15–18 h). Dilute 0.5 mg/mL stock 1:100 in sterile PBS, add 30 µL per well. Clean (or autoclave) a pair of extra‑fine scissors and two pairs of forceps for femur, tibia and spleen removal. Ready 15‑cm dishes for BMDM differentiation and 96‑well flat‑bottom plates for later seeding.

substeps.instruction: Plate coating: dilute antibody, add 30 µL/well, incubate 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Make BMDM culture medium
steps.instruction: Mix DMEM (+GlutaMAX) with 10 % heat‑inactivated fetal bovine serum (56 °C, 30 min) and 1 % Gentamicin (stock 50 mg/mL). Warm to 37 °C before use.

steps.title: Prepare inflammasome stimulation medium
steps.instruction: Collect murine serum from mice subjected to experimental stroke (fMCAO, 60 min ischemia; sacrifice 4 h after reperfusion). After intracardiac bleed, let blood clot 30 min at RT, centrifuge 3,500 g for 15 min, collect supernatant, aliquot and store at –80 °C. Add serum to BMDM medium to a final 25 % (v/v) concentration.

steps.title: Prepare T‑cell culture medium
steps.instruction: Mix RPMI‑1640 complete with 10 % FBS and 1 % Penicillin/Streptomycin (10 000 U/10 000 U stock). Add β‑mercaptoethanol to a final 5 nM concentration and warm to 37 °C.

steps.title: Select experimental mice
steps.instruction: Use C57BL/6J mice (6–12 weeks, both sexes) for bone‑marrow and serum collection. Optionally use B6 Actin‑eGFP (C57BL/6‑Tg(CAG‑EGFP)1Osb/J; JAX 003291) mice (≥8 weeks, both sexes) for GFP⁺ T‑cells.

steps.title: Isolate splenic T cells
steps.instruction: Euthanize a mouse, open the abdomen, expose and remove the spleen into 10 mL ice‑cold PBS. Mince spleen with scissors, press through a 40 µm strainer into a 50 mL conical tube, rinse with ≥10 mL PBS, bring volume to ≥20 mL and centrifuge 300 g for 10 min at RT. Resuspend pellet, count cells and adjust to 1 × 10⁷ cells per 100 µL. Add 20 µL T‑cell enrichment antibody cocktail per 100 µL, vortex 3×, incubate 10 min at RT. Bring volume to 4 mL with HBSS, wash 300 g for 8 min at RT. Discard supernatant, resuspend in 100 µL HBSS per 1 × 10⁷ cells. Add 20 µL magnetic‑bead‑labeled antibodies per 100 µL, vortex 3×, incubate 5 min at RT. Bring volume to 2.5 mL HBSS, place tube in the supplied magnet for 5 min at RT. Transfer the supernatant (enriched T cells) to a fresh 4 mL tube. Optional: keep the magnet‑bound fraction for QC by flow cytometry.

substeps.instruction: Spleen collection and storage in ice‑cold PBS.
Mincing and straining, wash and centrifuge.

steps.title: Seed T cells and start proliferation
steps.instruction: Wash enriched T cells 300 g for 8 min at RT. Count and resuspend to 3 × 10⁵ cells in 200 µL T‑cell medium per well. Add 200 µL to each anti‑CD3ε‑coated U‑bottom well. After 15 min at RT, add 10 µL CD28 antibody (0.1 µg/µL) per well. Incubate overnight (12–18 h) at 37 °C. Verify cell viability before proceeding to coculture.

steps.title: Prime BMDMs for inflammasome activation
steps.instruction: Dilute LPS to 100 ng/mL in BMDM medium, add to differentiated BMDMs and incubate 4 h at 37 °C. Optional visual check at 2 h for nuclear expansion and amoeboid morphology.

steps.title: Prepare T cells for coculture
steps.instruction: Pipette T cells from the U‑bottom wells into a 15 mL conical tube containing 2 mL pre‑warmed T‑cell medium. Centrifuge 300 g for 10 min at RT, discard supernatant, resuspend in 2 mL pre‑warmed T‑cell medium and adjust to 2 × 10⁵ T cells per well (or desired ratio, 1:1 to 1:8). Optional: keep cells on ice briefly before adding to BMDMs.

steps.title: Stimulate BMDMs with stroke serum
steps.instruction: Aspirate BMDM medium and immediately add inflammasome stimulation medium (BMDM medium + 25 % murine stroke serum). Incubate at 37 °C; serum typically activates the inflammasome within 15 min.

steps.title: Combine BMDMs and T cells (cell‑cell interaction)
steps.instruction: Remove the stimulation medium, wash BMDMs once with 200 µL serum‑free RPMI‑1640 complete medium. Add 100 µL serum‑free RPMI to each well, then add the prepared T‑cell suspension (2 × 10⁵ cells in 200 µL T‑cell medium) to reach a total volume of 300 µL per well. Optional: centrifuge the 96‑well plate at 300 g for 1 min to settle T cells onto BMDMs. Incubate at 37 °C for 2–6 h (or other desired time).

steps.title: Microscopy readout of T‑cell survival
steps.instruction: During the 180‑min interaction, acquire GFP images of predefined fields of view from each well. In ImageJ set fluorescence threshold, binarize images, and use ‘Analyze Particles’ with appropriate size and circularity settings to count GFP⁺ T cells per field. Export counts for statistical analysis.

steps.title: Flow‑cytometric analysis of cell death
steps.instruction: At 2–6 h after interaction, place the plate under laminar flow for the last 10 min at RT. Remove medium, wash wells with 1 mL HBSS, scrape cells and collect in 5 mL conical tubes. Bring volume to 2 mL HBSS on ice. Wash 300 g for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in 100 µL FACS staining buffer. Incubate 15 min on ice in the dark with 1 µL Fc blocker (0.5 µg/mL). Add antibody cocktail (each antibody 0.5 µg/mL), incubate 30 min in the dark at 4 °C. Bring volume to 2 mL with staining buffer, wash 300 g for 7 min; repeat wash once. Resuspend to 200 µL staining buffer and acquire on a flow cytometer, collecting 10 000 CD45⁺ events per sample. Gate macrophages (CD45⁺CD11b⁺F4/80⁺MHCII⁺) and T cells (CD45⁺CD11b⁻CD3⁺). Assess FasL⁺ (CD178) macrophages and T‑cell death using PI, Zombie or similar live/dead dyes. Optional: perform CFSE proliferation assay.

substeps.instruction: Timing: last 10 min of interaction at RT, then 15 min Fc block, 30 min antibody staining, 7 min washes.
